question: An engineer must perform backup and restore of the Cisco UCS Manager configuration. The configuration must be stored on a remote server via XML encoding. The backup must store the configurations of the chassis, FEX, rack servers, IOMs, and blade server. Which set of actions accomplishes these goals?
options: Perform an all configuration backup and run the system restore procedure.
Perform a full state configuration backup and run the restore procedure.
Perform a logical configuration backup and run the replace import method.
Perform a system configuration backup and run the merge import method.
theory: Backing up hardware-inventory-level configuration such as chassis, FEX, rack server, IOM, and blade server settings, stored on a remote server in XML format, corresponds to a System Configuration backup rather than Full State (binary, whole-system) or Logical Configuration (service profiles/VLANs/VSANs). When restoring that data into an existing environment, the merge import method combines the backed-up settings with the domain's current configuration instead of the replace method, which would wipe out existing configuration not present in the backup file — merge is the safer, additive restore approach appropriate here. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 14 — UCS Configuration Management, System Configuration Backup and Merge Import)
